nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Ru-S-NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, the metal precursors including 1188 mg NiCl2.6H2O, 450 mg FeCl3.6H2O, and 40 mg RuCl3 as well as 33.8 mg thiourea were completely dissolved in 16.66 mL DI water under continuously stirring for 30 min at first. Meanwhile, 1413 mg Na2CO3 was added in another beaker containing 13.33 mL DI water to form a homogeneous solution, followed with quickly pouring it into the former metal precursor solution. After stirring the mixed solution for 30 min, the mixture was added into the autoclave and aged in the oven at 100°C for 20 h. Finally, the brown precipitate was washed by water for five times and collected by centrifugation, and then dried in the vacuum oven at 80°C for 12 h to obtain the Ru-S-NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows Ru-S-NiFe LDH and NiFe LDH have identical Ni3Fe LDH phases (JCPDS No.40-0215) with enlarged lattice parameters for Ru-S-NiFe LDH: a=12.116 Å, b=6.317 Å, c=23.227 Å, V=1539.5 Å³.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the primary diffraction peaks located at ≈11.5°, 23.2°, 33.6°, 34.5°, 39.0°, 60.1°, and 60.6° are well ascribed to the (003), (006), (101), (012), (015), (110), and (113) facets of standard Ni3Fe LDH (JCPDS No.40-0215). Furthermore, fitting operations were conducted on these XRD patterns: the detailed lattice parameters are a = 12.112 Å, b = 6.313 Å, c = 23.220 Å and V = 1537.6 Å³ for NiFe LDH, as compared to a = 12.116 Å, b = 6.317 Å, c = 23.227 Å and V = 1539.5 Å³ for Ru-S-NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms CO3^2- at 1057 cm⁻¹; Ru-S-NiFe LDH shows decreased peak intensities, broadened widths, and slightly redshifted a1g (532 cm⁻¹) and eg (457, 300 cm⁻¹) peaks vs NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: all samples exhibit the similar Raman spectra, in which the Raman peak at 1057 cm⁻¹ proves the inserted anion in the interlayer is the CO₃²⁻... Ru-S-NiFe LDH displays decreased peak intensities, broaden peak widths, and slightly redshifted peak positions on these a1g and eg Raman peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM shows isolated Ru single atoms as bright spots due to Z-contrast.
nodes.evidence_snippet: aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark field-scanning TEM (AC HAADF-STEM) with atomic resolution was used... the bright spots with isolated dispersions can be clearly observed on the crystal support, demonstrating that the doped Ru species primarily exist as single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows Ru valence state +1.98 in Ru-S-NiFe LDH between Ru foil (0) and RuO2 (+4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the normalized Ru K-edge absorption energy edge position of Ru-S-NiFe LDH is located between the Ru foil and RuO2, implying the valence state of Ru species is between 0 and +4 in Ru-S-NiFe LDH... it is calculated that the Ru valence state in Ru-S-NiFe LDH and Ru-NiFe LDH are +1.98 and +3.58, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows main peak at 1.67 Å (Ru-O/S), no Ru-Ru (2.43 Å) or Ru-O-Ru (3.18 Å) peaks confirming atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru K-edge EXAFS results reveal that Ru-S-NiFe LDH only shows a main peak at ≈1.67 Å, the lack of a discernible Ru-Ru peak (2.43 Å) and Ru-O-Ru peak (3.18 Å) confirms the existence of single-atom Ru species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L2,3-edge sXAS confirms Ni²⁺ matching NiO reference; Fe L2,3-edge sXAS confirms Fe³⁺ matching Fe2O3 reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni L2,3 edge sXAS spectrum of Ru-S-NiFe LDH with NiO as the reference, their identical energy positions and spectra profiles can determine that Ni presents the oxidation state of +2 in Ru-S-NiFe LDH. Similarly... Fe L2,3 edge sXAS and Fe K-edge XANES spectra of Ru-S-NiFe LDH show the same profile and absorption energy edge position as the Fe2O3 reference.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows Ru 3p signals confirming Ru incorporation; S 2p shows S-O and S-Metal peaks; Ru 3p binding energy negatively shifts in Ru-S-NiFe LDH vs Ru-NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the survey XPS spectra clearly display the appearance of Ru 3p signals in both Ru-NiFe LDH and Ru-S-NiFe LDH... the S 2p XPS spectra of S-NiFe LDH and Ru-S-NiFe LDH can be deconvoluted as the S-O peak and S-Metal peak, respectively.

nodes.evidence_snippet: the elemental mappings in Figure 1h indicate that Ru, Ni, Fe, O, and S atoms are homogeneously dispersed over the whole Ru-S-NiFe LDH nanosheet.
